item.research_question: Can a phase prediction method for high-entropy alloys (HEAs) be developed by integrating a criterion and machine learning recommendation method?
key_findings: The proposed phase prediction of HEAs (PPH) achieves an average prediction accuracy of 91.6% in all HEAs.
The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 94.3% in quinary HEAs.
The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 93.1% in senary HEAs.
The PPH achieves an average prediction accuracy of 95.8% in septenary HEAs.
item.mechanism: The PPH combines the advantages of the criterion of SS and MLRM, where the criterion of SS has strong interpretability and generalization and requires only a small amount of training samples.
item.limitations: The performance of the meta-learner in traditional meta-learning is not ideal, and the KNN does not fully consider the information of the left and right nearest neighbors of every sample.
item.future_work: The PPH can also provide a research foundation in other material fields.
quotes: The comprehensive properties of high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are highly-dependent on their phases.
The PPH can achieve performance than the traditional meta-learning method.
The average prediction accuracy of the PPH in all, quinary, senary, and septenary HEAs is 91.6%, 94.3%, 93.1%, and 95.8%, respectively.
